summary: Preterit Intransitive permits zero-marked lexical nominal stimuli: definite craft i ṣənʕayo (Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/17), languages (MAC NE Interview 2/88; MAC how Ilyas learned/2,11), ʕəlm (24/257, already quoted), aġatiye (PrS 1/11). Thus avoidance of two zero-marked arguments cannot be categorical for ylf. Infinitival skill nouns provide additional, distinct evidence.

Other stimulus coding occurs with l- (Bilgic Der Beruf eines Kesselverzinkers/18; JL 9.9/11), b- (59/49; 60/10), and ʕal- (115/65). The adjacent 60/10–11 account alternates b-marked and zero-marked language nouns. Sources use me-/m- independently of stimulus marking.

Part act. expresses acquired skill or accustomed state, including past-copula yalifiwayna and yalífewayne. Preterit Intransitive can describe bounded acquisition, anterior competence or the acquisition of a habit. MAC how Ilyas learned/31 contrasts earlier yaləfno with incremental koyolafno.

Preterit-wa is provisionally supported by yalə́fwayno, yalifiwo, yaləfwo and yaləfínawo, against yulfínawo in Infectum-wa. Habitual versus anterior interpretations follow context; possible dialectal vowel levelling remains unresolved.

III varies zero-marked versus l-marked learners, with zero-marked curriculum or a clause; 97/13 contains two overt zero-marked internal arguments. Reduced məlfilan and kməlfanne remain III. Detransitive Infinitiv ilofo is the inherited formal allocation even where semantics is active learning.

Reader reports of an illness example being unnumbered and an English fragment indexed 66 are not borne out by this input: the Preterit Intransitive illness example already has sense 2 and the Preterit box has a single intact example. No nonexistent repair is proposed. Old prs page/line citations and supplied PrS text/verse numbering are retained as separate conventions, not silently substituted.

Round-1 I Preterit-wa and Infectum-wa and its III teaching examples are retained, so reader claims that these boxes are absent are stale. New l-agent III mawlaflewolan supports a distinct Preterit-wa box. I yləflan/yləfle are the inherited l-agent Preterit alternative.
I.2 includes explicit bad customs and lies with nominal stimuli and nonpayment with a d-clause. The plural article aʕ in aʕ ʕadat is not a stimulus preposition.

qal-type -wa forms frequently report retained expertise or habitual acquisition; context does not by itself settle Preterit-wa versus a locally levelled Infectum-wa. yulafwo and yulfiwa provide clearer Infectum-wa comparanda.

III literary authorship contrasts with teaching. Three bibliographical contexts support sense 2, but repeated tokens in 299 and 316 are not independent attestations. Arabic-contact or learned etymological reassignment needs editorial review.

məlfiwo is provisionally III Detransitive Preterit-wa with retained language content; its supplied English uses active had learned and is not morphological evidence. No repair of the alleged sense66 fragment is proposed: the input has one intact inherited Preterit example.

ylf I Part act. sense 1 is already amply covered after round 1; no further routine state examples were added. Supplied routine_counts summarize additional attestations and require no occurrence lines.
Confirm qaṭəl-based Preterit-wa versus locally levelled Infectum-wa in MAC Ishaq Material culture/18 and MAC YT LIFE STORY/32–33,45,64.

Confirm segmentation of III məlfilan (Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/56), molúffallan (MAC YT LIFE STORY/10) and dmolafli (MAC how Ilyas learned/14); the last remains unquoted because teacher/pupil and clause analysis are unresolved.
Does -yo in moláfleliyo (MAC how Ilyas learned/20) resume Arabic, serve as a particle, or have another function? Is yaləfne (MAC Hanna Dewo/12) 1sg plus object -e?
Confirm d-stimulus analysis of yalifo du nušuk / di qaḥwa and whether negative evaluation alone licenses sense 2; neutral coffee/snuff familiarity is retained under sense 1.
The inherited Infinitiv example contains the apparent heading fragment ilofo; 659; within its Turoyo field. Confirm the source layout before separating it; retain the supplied text meanwhile.

Confirm qaṭəl-wa versus dialectal Infectum-wa in yaləfiwo/yəlfinawo/yəlfituwo and whether -le in Yaləfiwole and Yləfwolle is a stimulus clitic or l-agent. The learner in 1879 is male; the reader feminine morphological label there is not accepted.
At Jan 3.1/19 is məlfiwo a III Detransitive Preterit-wa form or a lexical educated predicate with a past copula? The box/example remains provisional.
Should III authorship be a separate homonym of Arabic origin rather than sense 2 of ylf? The meanings are kept distinct pending etymological review.
At Jan 4.II/934 does getting accustomed to lak kallat carry the negative evaluation needed for I.2, or is it neutral I.1? The money rendering alone does not decide this.
At Jan 1.35/1430 who is the experiencer, and is ḥa mam məḏyoye its stimulus or subject? At Jan 3.49/1353 does masculine-shaped ylaf address the daughter or quote another speaker?
Animal experiencers (ox, fox, camel) and acquired craft expertise remain within learning/neutral habituation; instrument or profession nouns may name a learned skill metonymically.
Teaching includes animal training and military instruction; these do not require new senses.
Jan independently supports the round-1 zero-marked nominal-stimulus finding: lišone; naqəš; qraye w kṯawto, and qaṭəl-wa craft nouns. These do not create another sense.
Substantivized yalife names learned people in the written biographical register; retain the acquired-knowledge interpretation already supported in round 1.
Possible human-stimulus extension in yaləfwo ḥa mam məḏyoye remains unresolved because the bare NP could be subject. No hire or acquaintance sense is established.
